I found the bug.

**File:** `src/cachetools/_cached.py`, function `_wrapper` (lines 229–259).

**Cause:** When `info is None` (the default, no `maxsize`/no stats tracking requested), the code checks `if not cache:` (line 242) to decide whether to use the cached path. But `not cache` is `True` whenever the cache is empty (e.g. a freshly created `LRUCache(maxsize=8)` or an empty `dict`), not just when `cache is None`. So on a fresh cache, `_wrapper` picks the `_uncached` wrapper, which never reads or writes the cache — matching the bug report symptom exactly (computed every time, `len(cache)` stays 0).

Contrast with the `info is not None` branch (line 231), which correctly uses `if cache is None:`.

**Fix:** Change line 242 from `if not cache:` to `if cache is None:` so that the caching path is selected whenever a cache object (even an empty one) was passed, and only the explicit "no cache" (`cache=None`) case uses `_uncached`.
